figures.caption: Table 6: Hidden-state shifts relative to NL-only. Larger shifts do not necessarily imply higher pass rates.

Figure 2: Paired behavioral and task-level representational analyses. (a) Pass-rate advantage of relevant public tests over shuffledoutput and irrelevant-test controls. (b) Advantage of relevant tests over NL-only prompting on LiveCodeBench, stratified by model and task difficulty. Points in (a–b) show paired percentage-point differences; bars show 95% Newcombe score intervals. (c) Mean hidden-state shift by behavioral outcome after residualizing average non-embedding-layer cosine distance on added prompt characters within each run and condition and standardizing the residuals. Bars in (c) show exploratory 95% task-clustered bootstrap intervals.
Table 2: Behavior flips between prompt conditions. A gain means the base condition fails and the target condition passes. Exact two-sided McNemar tests use the discordant gain/loss counts.

Figure 1: Overview of the main behavioral and representational findings. Public tests improve MBPP+ but have weak or unstable effects on HumanEval+ and recent LiveCodeBench tasks. In the behavior panel, MB, HE, L7, and L27 denote MBPP+, HumanEval+, and LiveCodeBench with the 7B and 27B checkpoints; rel., shuf., irr., and syn. denote relevant, shuffled, irrelevant, and synthetic-high5 tests. Hidden-state shifts show that larger prompt-induced representation changes can occur without corresponding correctness gains.
